articles.title: David Sánchez señala el gran problema del Barcelona tras perder ante el Real Madrid: "Se lo tiene que hacer mirar"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco reconoce en La Tribu la superioridad táctica de Mourinho sobre Flick en el Clásico
articles.summary: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco reconoce en La Tribu la superioridad táctica de Mourinho sobre Flick en el Clásico
articles.body: La derrota del Barcelona ante el Real Madrid en el Spotify Camp Nou ha dejado muchas lecturas. Una de ellas, la de David Sánchez, que en su intervención en La Tribu de Radio MARCA no ha puesto ningún reparo al triunfo del conjunto blanco y ha señalado directamente los problemas que está mostrando el equipo de Hansi Flick en los partidos de máxima exigencia. "Nada que objetar a la victoria del Real Madrid ante el Barcelona ayer en el Spotify Camp Nou", ha comenzado asegurando David Sánchez, que ha reconocido el acierto del técnico madridista en su planteamiento. "Mourinho le ganó la partida a Hansi Flick porque le sorprendió, porque fue valiente y porque, sobre todo, desactivó el centro del campo del Barcelona, al que formaron Rodri, Fermín y Pedri", ha explicado el periodista. David Sánchez ha puesto el foco en una circunstancia que empieza a preocupar en el conjunto azulgrana: "El Barcelona se tiene que hacer mirar las noches importantes, los días en los cuales te la juegas ante los grandes rivales", ha advertido. Y es que el periodista ha recordado los dos últimos tropiezos del equipo de Flick: "Y en una semana has palmado contra el PSG y has palmado en casa ante el Real Madrid de José Mourinho". Dos derrotas que, a juicio de David Sánchez, obligan al técnico alemán a reflexionar sobre determinados aspectos de su propuesta futbolística, especialmente cuando el nivel de exigencia aumenta. Pese a las críticas, David Sánchez mantiene su confianza en el potencial del conjunto azulgrana. "Hay tiempo para rectificar, aunque da la sensación de que Hansi Flick no va a renunciar a su estilo", ha señalado. El periodista ha cerrado su reflexión con un mensaje claro sobre el principal aspecto que debe mejorar el Barcelona: "El Barcelona es un gran equipo, pero tiene, repito, que retocar ciertos registros defensivos en las noches en las cuales te juegan los títulos ante los equipos grandes en Europa y en España". Un toque de atención de David Sánchez después de una semana marcada por las derrotas ante el PSG y el Real Madrid, en la que el Barça ha vuelto a mostrar, según su análisis, sus dificultades para competir en las grandes citas.

articles.title: Mourinho, el terror del Camp Nou
articles.standfirst: Mou vuelve a conquistar el estadio azulgrana, resuelve a lo grande un mes envenenado y firma cinco triunfos seguidos que catapultan al Madrid
articles.summary: Mou vuelve a conquistar el estadio azulgrana, resuelve a lo grande un mes envenenado y firma cinco triunfos seguidos que catapultan al Madrid
articles.body: El Camp Nou tenía motivos para temer a Mou. El regreso del técnico a Barcelona, otra vez al frente del Real Madrid, no sólo generaba una gran expectación, también cierto recelo entre muchos aficionados azulgrana que no se fiaban. No era la primera vez que el luso ponía patas arriba el estadio azulgrana y esa preocupación reinaba en el ambiente del Barça. Y Mou lo volvió a hacer. Conquistó por cuarta vez el Camp Nou y no lo hizo de cualquier manera. Con todo en contra, con medio título en juego, con bajas importantes... El Real Madrid de Mou jugaba una 'final' en Barcelona tras un comienzo de Liga en el que la mezcla de traspiés de los blancos y la imperial marcha triunfal de los de Flick habían puesto al Madrid contra las cuerdas en el campeonato doméstico. El Clásico era un todo o nada. Y salió cara para el Madrid, que confirmó en el Camp Nou que está de vuelta y que el equipo ha cogido velocidad de crucero. De hecho, el triunfo ante el Barça tiene muchos componentes para ser considerado un punto de inflexión para el Madrid. Amplían su mejor racha de la temporada hasta los cinco triunfos seguidos, acaba con la condición de invicto de los azulgrana en Liga, rebajan la alarma quedándose a sólo tres puntos, asaltan el Camp Nou y endosan la segunda derrota seguida del Barça, tras la del PSG en Champions, y rubrican un mes de octubre envenenado con una matrícula de honor tras cinco triunfos: tres en Liga y dos en Champions. El Madrid arregla la delicada situación que tenía en Liga y consolida su fortaleza en Champions, donde cuenta las jornadas por triunfos. Y todo ello con Mou de protagonista. “Los chicos han hecho un partido extraordinario, muy organizados, concentrados, con coraje para salir jugando desde atrás con un adversario que presiona mucho. Ganamos a un gran adversario y con un árbitro que lo ha hecho bien y un VAR que estaba dormido en el minuto 60, en una clara tarjeta roja de Cancelo a Diomande. Pero gran partido y gran victoria”, apuntó Mou.

articles.title: Álvaro Benito subraya la realidad de "perogrullo" y la "lección" que han sacado Mou y el Madrid del Clásico
articles.standfirst: "Me lleváis años escuchando siempre lo mismo. No soy dudoso. Ser jugador de talento no te exime de que puedas hacer un ejercicio defensivo como requiere la alta competición"
articles.summary: "Me lleváis años escuchando siempre lo mismo. No soy dudoso. Ser jugador de talento no te exime de que puedas hacer un ejercicio defensivo como requiere la alta competición"
articles.body: Álvaro Benito, futbolista del Real Madrid de 1995 a 2002 que se vio obligado a retirarse del fútbol en 2003 por culpa de las lesiones, analizó en el programa 'Carrusel Deportivo' las claves del Clásico que el Real Madrid acabó ganando 1-2 al F.C. Barcelona. El ex futbolista de 49 años, que venía semanas antes de diagnosticar los males del Madrid y pedir "decisiones drásticas", reconoció que "me lleváis años escuchando siempre lo mismo. No soy dudoso. Ser jugador de talento o de más talento no te exime de que puedas hacer un ejercicio defensivo como requiere la alta competición y los equipos top. Ahora mismo, sin eso, no puedes ser competitivo". Álvaro Benito subrayó la personalidad y capacidad de sacrificio que mostró el Real Madrid en el Spotify Camp Nou: "El Madrid... ¿Por qué ha atacado bien? Porque ha defendido bien también. Todos han corrido y han tenido un plan defensivo en el que nadie se ha saltado las normas; han sido agresivos y a partir de ahí han atacado bien porque defiendes bien. Cuando defiendes bien, robas mucho más balón, el rival se le incomoda y tú vas a tener más cuota de pelota, y con los jugadores que tienes puedes hacer mucho daño". El ex de Real Madrid, Valladolid, Getafe y Tenerife destacó la presencia de Bernardo Silva en el 11 inicial que sacó Mourinho en Barcelona. "Todo esto que estoy diciendo es superobvio, es de perogrullo, pero que no se estaba cumpliendo. Y creo que este es el 11 ahora mismo. Bernardo puede jugar de mediocentro en un partido top perfectamente si todos curran. Ante la elección de Bernardo, a priori, sabía que le había elegido para salir de la presión del Barça y no tanto para dominar. Creo que Mourinho tampoco esperaba un partido de dominar mucho, pero sí es ese tipo de jugador que ante la presión del Barça no le quema el balón, te recibe de espaldas, te amaga y te puede sacar una jugada limpia. Esa es la lección. Y Bernardo es necesario ahora mismo para el juego del equipo, porque dentro no tienes esa fluidez, esa finura, contra equipos top que te vayan a presionar", analizó el exfutbolista de 49 años en declaraciones que reproduce la web de la Cadena SER. Álvaro Benito tiene claro que "a partir de aquí. Más allá de esto, este es el camino. Todo lo que no sea repetir esto y que Mourinho lo tiene fácil... El Barça venía imparable, han hecho un grandísimo partido, han ganado el Camp Nou, se han metido de nuevo en la pelea. No vale deshacer el camino andado, porque pienso que esto tiene que ser el punto de partida sobre lo que construir la temporada del Real Madrid. A partir de aquí, este Real Madrid es competitivo en cualquier competición. Este, sí. Lo que habíamos visto hasta entonces, en mi opinión, no". Álvaro Benito también habló del juego del F.C. Barcelona y del estilo de Hansi Flick, apuntando a uno de los puntos débiles del equipo culé: "Tampoco soy dudoso en lo que voy a decir. Llevo diciendo años que Flick, que me encanta como entrenador, pero creo que el Barça, contra los equipos buenos, que más o menos tienen un día medio normal, se van a presentar cuatro o cinco veces delante de tu portero. Todos los equipos de nivel te lo van a hacer y es muy difícil que los equipos buenos no te encuentren eso. Sigue arriesgando demasiado en ciertos aspectos y es un equipo que da gusto verlo y que a la mayoría de los equipos los destruye por ese ritmo alto, por la presión y porque no tienen la calidad para penalizar esa defensa tan adelantada. Pero el Real Madrid, sí. Porque el Real Madrid ha estado muy mal en el último pase, en la última toma de decisión, pero ha tenido cuatro o cinco situaciones que jugadores de ese nivel como Bellingham o Mbappé deberían haber resuelto mejor".

articles.title: Ballon d'Or: Will Lamine Yamal, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe or Lionel Messi win?
articles.summary: The Ballon d'Or winner will be announced in London on Monday - but who is going to claim the showpiece award?
articles.body:
The Ballon d'Or winner will be announced in London on 26 October - but who is going to win it?

Bookmakers have Spain winger Lamine Yamal and England captain Harry Kane very close together as clear favourites.

Lamine Yamal won La Liga with Barcelona and the World Cup with Spain, while Kane scored 73 goals for German champions Bayern Munich and England.

Eight-time winner Lionel Messi, of Argentina and Inter Miami, and Real Madrid's France forward Kylian Mbappe are the other probable candidates.

Or how about one of Paris St-Germain's back-to-back European champions?

BBC Sport asked several of its football experts who they think should take home the award.

Goal, assist... goal-kick - Kane underlines Ballon d'Or credentials

Lamine Yamal 'completes football' at 19 as Argentina betray Messi

How PSG's Ballon d'Or duo are pushing each other on

European football expert Guillem Balague: Can you imagine this Ballon d'Or not won by a PSG player or a Spanish player? Impossible. So gone is Kylian Mbappe.

The PSG players, there are so many of them that deserve it - Fabian Ruiz, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Ousmane Dembele, Vitinha. So the vote is going to be split.

There is only one Spaniard who deserves it, and that's Lamine Yamal, who has given us individual performances, collective trophies, and has that aura. He's going to win it.

European football expert Julien Laurens: I think he was the best player in Europe last season, especially in the Champions League where he was outstanding. He helped lead the team to another title, a back-to-back one.

He got the penalty in the final, scored in both semi-finals, in the quarter-final, and in the last 16. He was amazing in those huge, huge games where you want your best players to step up. He deserves to win the Ballon d'Or for being the best player in the world all the way up to the World Cup.

He won't win it, unfortunately, because Lamine Yamal, for the player he is and how entertaining and spectacular he is, didn't really shine at the World Cup, even if Spain won it. He didn't really do that well in the Champions League for Barcelona, getting knocked out early. However, his style of football means he'll probably win it - but it should be Kvaratskhelia.

Ex-Liverpool and Blackburn full-back Stephen Warnock : I think it will be Lamine Yamal for helping Spain to win the World Cup. If you were asking who else is in the hunt, I would say Michael Olise, but my pick personally would be Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, he is unbelievable. I love watching him play. He had such an impact for Paris St-Germain and last season he was incredible. I just don't think he will get the votes with Georgia not being in the World Cup.

BBC Radio 5 Live Euro Leagues guest and Athletic reporter Rory Smith: It will probably go to Lamine Yamal because it generally goes to someone who has won the biggest trophy, and this is the World Cup. It shouldn't be him because he wasn't necessarily Spain's most important player but his fame and talent means it will be him.

Personally I would give it to Kvaratskhelia. He has been the most exciting player in European club football for a while now, a valuable part of the PSG team who retained the Champions League, and crucially I think you shouldn't suffer because you come from a country who isn't in the running to win the World Cup.

Former England striker Alan Shearer: The winner of the Ballon d'Or should be Harry Kane. His numbers for the last 12 to 18 months have been absolutely sensational for Bayern and for England. For that reason, he should get it.

Ex-England midfielder Danny Murphy: My choice for the Ballon d'Or is Harry Kane. I think his goalscoring has been relentless, brilliant. He's had one of the best seasons of his career and it'll be a great reward for him if he gets the trophy. He's been brilliant at Bayern Munich since he's been there, adapted really well and he's been the best centre-forward in the world for the last 12 months.

Former Tottenham and Crystal Palace forward Andros Townsend : Harry Kane should win the Ballon d'Or. He scored 73 goals in 65 games, 36 of those in the Bundesliga. He led Bayern Munich to the league and cup double. He scored 14 goals in the Champions League, helping Bayern Munich to the semi-finals and scored six goals in the World Cup, leading England to the semi-finals. He has had an outstanding year.

Former England striker Ellen White : It's a tough one but I'll go with my heart - I'd love to see Harry Kane win it. I know he didn't win the World Cup but his numbers are absolutely extraordinary, with what he has achieved with Bayern Munich and England. Lamine Yamal had a few injuries but I know he won the World Cup and I'm sure he will win the Ballon d'Or one day. Michael Olise has also been phenomenal.

Norwegian football journalist Lars Sivertsen on Champions League Match of the Day: I would like to see Harry Kane win it, he deserves it. He is a real leader at Bayern Munich. He never makes trouble and is a role model. But I do wonder if him being a low-key character hurts him. The Ballon d'Or is a popularity contest. I love that he doesn't do all that but maybe he should.

articles.title: Hoy es el Balón de Oro: el 'campeón' Lamine Yamal versus Kane, Messi, Mbappé...
articles.standfirst: El crack de la Selección campeona del mundo es ligeramente favorito en un 'Ballon d'Or' muy abierto
articles.summary: El crack de la Selección campeona del mundo es ligeramente favorito en un 'Ballon d'Or' muy abierto
articles.body: Londres será, por el 70 aniversario del primer Balón en 1956, el escenario elegido por ‘France Football’ para la entrega del ‘Ballon D’Or’ de este año, aunque el periodo futbolístico que se juzga comprende desde el 31 de julio de 2025 (después del Mundial de Clubes) hasta el 1 de agosto de 2026 (incluye el Mundial absoluto ganado por España). Será esta noche a las 21.00 en España (Movistar en directo desde las 19.30 horas). Posiblemente, sea el Balón de Oro más imprevisible de los últimos años. Es cierto que el campeonato del mundo ganado por La Roja le da un ligero favoritismo a Lamine Yamal, por delante de los otros tres grandes candidatos: Harry Kane, capitán de Inglaterra, tercera en el Mundial; Lionel Messi, capitán de la Argentina finalista; y un Kylian Mbappé que terminó mal el Mundial con Francia (cuarto puesto)... y que no obtuvo ningún título con el Real Madrid en el periodo juzgado. Sin embargo, batió algunos récords importantes a nivel individual (en goles) tanto en la historia de los Mundiales (ya es el máximo goleador de las Copas del Mundo), como en la Champions League 25-26. El desafío para Lamine es histórico. Si lo gana, conseguiría su primer Balón de Oro a los 19 años, tres meses y 13 días de edad, el jugador más joven en conseguirlo en los 70 años de historia de este prestigioso galardón. El jugador más precoz hasta ahora es Ronaldo Nazario, que lo obtuvo en 1997 con 21 años, tres meses y 96 días de edad. Harry Kane podría ser tan favorito como Lamine, si bien la diferencia entre uno y otro en la pasada Copa del Mundo debería... hacer la diferencia. Pero es algo muy difícil de pronosticar. Las casas de apuesta han cacareado el favoritismo del inglés, anteponiendo los espectaculares registros goleadores de HK en todos los torneos (73 goles en 65 partidos entre Bayern y Selección) a un Lamine que es campeón del mundo, y campeón de la Supercopa de España y de la Liga con una excepcional actuación en ambas... pero al que le puede penalizar el hecho de haber llegado lesionado al Mundial y no haber sido el mejor de La Roja, un concepto que sí fue premiado por la propia FIFA para Unai Simón(mejor portero; Cubarsí (mejor joven) y Rodri (MVP). Aun así, Lamine es el símbolo mediático, la estrella, el crack y la luz de esta Roja, en general, y por ello también cuenta con muchas opciones de ganar este Balón de Oro. Si fuera por títulos, eso sí, el premio sería para Fabián Ruiz (Ligue 1, Champions y Mundial), pero también estuvo lesionado muchos meses. Y luego, más allá del caso particular del galo Mbappé, está la ‘vía Messi’, nada descartable por muchos. Leo —ayer ni nos confirmaban ni nos descartaban su presencia hoy en Londres— tiene a favor ser quien es (para muchos, el más grande de la historia), haber ganado la MLS con el Inter y un Mundial casi perfecto a sus 39 años. No es fácil elegir pues, pero en España se decantan por el favoritismo de Lamine pues se cree que el fútbol no puede cometer, de nuevo, el error de 2010 cuando el esplendoroso Mundial de España no se vio reflejado en un Balón de Oro para Iniesta o Xavi Hernández —fue para Messi aquel año—. ¿Se cometerá de nuevo el mismo ‘desliz’? El impoluto Mundial de La Roja hará que, al margen del Balón de Oro masculino, puede que caiga algún otro premio dentro de las restantes categorías que se premiarán hoy. Esas categorías son: Trofeo Kopa al mejor talento de la temporada (Lamine yPau Cubarsí optan); Trofeo Yashin al mejor portero (el español Unai Simón es uno de los grandes favoritos, aunque también están nominados Courtois, Joan García yDavid Raya); Trofeo Johan Cruyff al mejor entrenador (De la Fuente es el favorito por delante del ganador de la Champions, Luis Enrique, Emery o Arteta); y Trofeo Gerd Müller al mejor delantero (Kane es el favorito). La suerte está echada. Hoy, a las 21.00, la solución.

articles.title: El Balón de Oro podría teñirse de azulgrana
articles.standfirst: Las categorías femeninas tienen claro tinte azulgrana con Alexia Putellas, Cata Coll o Pere Romeu como claros favoritos en sus categorías
articles.summary: Las categorías femeninas tienen claro tinte azulgrana con Alexia Putellas, Cata Coll o Pere Romeu como claros favoritos en sus categorías
articles.body: El Barcelona no es sólo el mejor club según el ranking UEFA, sino que es el actual referente del fútbol mundial. El conjunto azulgrana firmó un histórico póker de títulos la temporada pasada (Liga, Copa, Supercopa de España, Champions League) que le hacen ser el claro favorito en todas las categoría del Balón de Oro, cuya gala se celebrará este lunes en el London Palladium Theatre. Alexia Putellas, dos veces galardonada con el Balón de Oro (2021, 2022), parte como principal favorita para llevarse nuevamente el trofeo después de haberlo ganado todo tanto con el Barcelona como con la selección española, siendo MVP de la Champions League y de la Nations League. Además de la de Mollet del Vallès, la lista de 30 candidatas cuenta en nómina con otras cinco españolas: Patri Guijarro, bien colocada en las quinielas previas; Claudia Pina, Cata Coll, Mariona Caldentey y Mapi León. Más allá de las españolas, hay otras tres futbolistas azulgrana en la lista: Ewa Pajor, Caroline Graham y Esmee Brugts. Cata Coll parte como principal candidata a llevarse el premio a 'Mejor Guardameta del año' (Trofeo Yashin), galardón por el que compite con Ann-Katrin Kerber, Hannah Hampton, Lorena y Ayaka Yamashita. En lo que al premio a 'Mejor Jugadora Joven del año' (Trofeo Kopa) se refiere, las azulgrana Vicky López y Clara Serrajordi compiten con Felicia Schröder -hoy jugadora del Real Madrid-, Lily Yohannes y Veerle Buurman. Como equipo, el Barcelona competirá por ser nombrado como 'Mejor club femenino del año' ante el Bayern de Múnich, Manchester City, OL Lyonnes y Club América. Por su parte, Pere Romeu, técnico azulgrana, competirá con su antecesor en el banquillo del Barcelona -ahora en el OL Lyonnes-, Jonatan Giráldez, además de con Andrée Jeglertz, Nils Nielsen y Elena Sadiku en el premio a 'Mejor Entrenador/a del año' (Trofeo Johan Cruyff). Cabe recordar que el jurado del Balón de Oro para la categoría femenina consta de 50 miembros, uno por país de los cincuenta primeros del ranking FIFA, siendo quien escribe (MARCA) el representante español.

articles.title: El Balón de Oro se muda a Londres: el London Palladium, el escenario de una noche histórica
articles.standfirst: La capital británica ya se prepara para una gala irrepetible, en la que el Balón de Oro cumple 70 años y ha elegido un teatro cargado de historia para celebrarlo
articles.summary: La capital británica ya se prepara para una gala irrepetible, en la que el Balón de Oro cumple 70 años y ha elegido un teatro cargado de historia para celebrarlo
articles.body: El Balón de Oro romperá este año con una de sus tradiciones más arraigadas. Después de décadas ligado a París, el galardón individual más prestigioso del fútbol mundial cruzará el Canal de la Mancha para celebrar su 70ª edición en el corazón de Londres. El próximo 26 de octubre, el mítico London Palladium se convertirá en la capital mundial del balón. No se trata de una mudanza definitiva ni de un cambio de sede permanente del Théâtre du Châtelet de París. La decisión responde a un motivo profundamente simbólico: rendir homenaje a Sir Stanley Matthews, el primer futbolista que levantó el Balón de Oro en 1956. Siete décadas después de aquel hito, los organizadores han querido que la gala viaje hasta Inglaterra para recordar al hombre que inauguró la historia del premio. Creado por la revista francesa France Football en 1956, el Balón de Oro celebra este año un aniversario redondo con su traslado a la capital británica. Desde 2024, la organización corre a cargo conjuntamente de France Football y UEFA, una alianza que ha reforzado el carácter global del evento. La gala tendrá lugar en uno de los recintos más icónicos del Reino Unido. El London Palladium. Situado en Argyll Street, en pleno West End, abrió sus puertas en 1910 y es una institución cultural británica. Por su escenario han pasado artistas de la talla de Frank Sinatra, The Beatles, Adele, Elton John o Coldplay. Con capacidad para 2.286 espectadores, el Palladium recibirá a buena parte de la élite del fútbol mundial. Estarán presentes los nominados al Balón de Oro masculino y femenino, representantes de los clubes, entrenadores, dirigentes de UEFA y de France Football, además de leyendas del fútbol e invitados del mundo del espectáculo. Entre los candidatos al premio masculino figuran nombres como Kylian Mbappé, Erling Haaland, Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Lamine Yamal, Rodri, Lionel Messi... lo que garantiza una de las alfombras rojas más espectaculares de los últimos años. El fútbol conocerá ese 26 de octubre a los herederos de Ousmane Dembélé y Aitana Bonmatí, vigentes ganadores de los premios masculino y femenino, respectivamente.

articles.title: Descifran los insultos y amenazas de Neymar en su expulsión por la 'Ley Vinicius'
articles.standfirst: Neymar fue expulsado después de que Rodrigo Nestor (Bahía) denunciase al árbitro que se había tapado la boca para insultarle
articles.summary: Neymar fue expulsado después de que Rodrigo Nestor (Bahía) denunciase al árbitro que se había tapado la boca para insultarle
articles.body: Neymar, delantero del Santos, fue expulsado por taparse la boca mientras discutía con Rodrigo Nestor (Bahía) en un partido correspondiente a la trigésima segunda jornada del Campeonato Brasileño que terminó con empate 1-1. El árbitro es llamado por el VAR y el ex de Barcelona y PSG es expusado con roja directa al considerar el colegiado que Neymar incumplía la bautizada 'Ley Vinícius Júnior' que se aplica en el 'Brasileirão'. "Neymar sabe lo que me dijo. Fue una falta de respeto hacia mí y hacia la camiseta del Bahía. Es un ídolo para todo el mundo como jugador, pero hoy falló como persona por la forma en que habló. No se deben hacer ese tipo de cosas. Mis padres me educaron muy bien y les agradezco la educación que me dieron. Yo nunca diría algo así", declaró Rodrigo Néstor en el descanso del partido. La polémica se agudizó después de que Velloso, especialista en lectura labial, interpretase en sus redes sociales lo que le dijo Neymar a Rodrigo Nestor. "Eres una mierda. Eres una mierda, pedazo de cabrón. Eres una mierda, cabrón, eres un imbécil. Pedazo de mierda", le dice Neymar a Rodrigo Néstor, que anteriormente le dijo "oye, quítame las manos de encima". Tras este rifirrafe el árbitro le sacó tarjeta amarilla a Neymar. Poco después Rodrigo Nestor le dijo a Kike Oliveira que "Neymar me llamó mierda. Que soy una mierda y que, además, me merezco estar en el equipo en el que estoy". "Exacto. Digo lo que quiero. Digo lo que quiero", le dijo Neymar al jugador de Bahía en declaraciones que reproduce 'Globo Sporte'. Tras el descanso, y las declaraciones a la prensa de Rodrigo Néstor, Neymar volvió a la carga en Vila Belmiro. "Oye, te voy a agarrar; ya verás si no te agarro", le amenazó Neymar a Rodrigo Néstor. "¡Oiga, oiga! Se ha tapado la boca con la mano", denunció el jugador de Bahía al árbitro. "No vas a hacer eso. ¿Quieres llamar la atención?", se quejó Neymar... que fue expulsado por la 'Ley Vinicius'. Tras ver la tarjeta roja Neymar fue a por Rodrigo Nestor, quien fue protegido por sus compañeros de equipo. "Ven aquí, hijo de puta", le grito Neymar al futbolista del Bahía. Antes de abandonar el terreno de juego Neymar escuchó a su compañero Rodinei la promesa de que le haría una entrada a Nestor antes de que terminara el partido: "Voy a ir a por él, voy a ir a por él. Ten por seguro que voy a ir a por él. Le voy a hacer una entrada". Tras el partido Neymar recurrió a sus redes redes sociales para dar su versión de los hechos en relación a su polémica con Rodrigo Nestor. "Normalmente no hablo de lo que pasa en el partido, especialmente cuando es una discusión entre jugadores, y yo terminé expulsado. Pero hoy fue algo muy serio, creo que fue más allá, ¿saben? Defiendo esto, daría mi vida por esto, les gritaría a todos, pelearía, discutiría, todo está bien. Pero después del partido, cada uno sigue su camino y todo está bien. Tiene que defender a su equipo, pero esto es fútbol. Esto es fútbol, no se puede hacer eso", denunció Neymar. El ex del Barcelona siguió atacando directamente a Rodrigo Néstor: "Ni siquiera me gusta hacer esto, hablar de estas cosas, todo está bien. Si cometo un error, estoy aquí para afrontar las consecuencias. Pero él (Rodrigo Nestor) dijo que no puede repetir lo que le dije porque hay niños mirando. Vi una entrevista donde dijo que yo le insulté. Hermano, le di con la pelota en la cintura y fingió que le golpeó en la cara. ¿Qué clase de ejemplo quiere dar? Habló de educación, yo también soy educado. Y, además, soy un hombre, lo que hiciste, no se debe hacer". "Y a quien haya creado esta ley (la 'Ley Vinicius'), que tenga cuidado, porque da cabida a la deshonestidad en el terreno de juego y luego pasa esto que me pasó a mí. Una vez más, yo soy un ejemplo. No hice una mierda. Me voy a casa, enfadado porque cometí un error: le di a un idiota la oportunidad de hacerse notar. Gracias, Nestor, yo dormiré tranquilo, pero tú, con tus mentiras, no lo harás. Esta ley es contra el racismo, no para que la uses en tu beneficio", le dedicó al futbolista del Bahía.

articles.title: Yousef Salech hails Jack Moylan partnership for Cardiff City
articles.summary: Yousef Salech believes he and Jack Moylan are proving mutually beneficial amid Cardiff City's improved Championship fortunes.
articles.body:
Yousef Salech believes he and Jack Moylan are proving mutually beneficial as Cardiff City improve their Championship fortunes.

Salech scored the winner against Birmingham on Saturday after being included as a late starting change following a five-week injury absence.

Cardiff planned to use him for a maximum 45 minutes, but he lasted the full 90 in atrocious conditions, while summer signing Moylan also played his part in the win.

"I love playing with Jack. I hope he feels the same," said Salech.

"He's more mobile than me, but probably I suck in more defenders closer to me and give him space so I hope and think we both benefit from playing with each other when we do."

Salech ends Birmingham's unbeaten run on Cardiff return

Cardiff's Aberfan inspiration after emotional tribute

Salech's deft winner came in the 31st minute, making the most of Ollie Tanner's assist for the Dane's goal third in the league since the Bluebird's return to the second-tier for 2026-27.

Ex-Birmingham player Krystian Bielik was stood down shortly before kick off after suffering a groin issue during the warm-up, prompting Salech's promotion to the starting line-up "two-and-half minutes" before kick off.

Before grabbing the games only goal, last season's top scorer had earlier seen his penalty attempt saved by Blues keeper James Beadle.

"I think the best thing as a player is to see it as any other chance in the game. I've missed a lot of chances in a lot of games. I've also missed penalties before," added Salech.

"But that's not going to end the game. There's still 70 minutes left to play."

The build-up to Saturday's encounter was filled with emotion, with boss Brian Barry-Murphy highlighting the importance of a fitting performance as they marked the Aberfan disaster of 1966.

In the week before facing Birmingham, the Cardiff City squad and management visited Aberfan, taking in the graveyard where 116 children and 28 adults who died in the catastrophe are buried.

Salech said: "First of all, I wasn't really educated or aware of this historic event before this week, but Brian and all of the staff of the club have informed us on Monday and we've seen almost a whole movie about it and also spoken between players."

He added: "It was very emotional to get out there and see the memorial and speak to people who were involved and who were there that day that happened and speaking about their beloved ones and classmates and family members and everything.

"And obviously I think it had a big impact on us on Tuesday and towards the build up towards the game... it seemed as though there was that little bit extra bite in every tackle, every chase for the ball.

"That comes from a team doing well anyway, but I just thought if that had played a little bit into it, it could have."

Miguel Torres, ex del Real Madrid, destacó en 'Radioestadio Noche' que "a Mourinho se le ha dado la autoridad que no se le dio a Xabi Alonso". articles.title: Longstaff almost produces silencer - Graham Smyth's Verdict on Sunderland 0-0 Leeds United
articles.summary: Greatest league in the world it may be but the Premier League still has its instant forgettables and this was one.The trampoline sitting beside the main road...
articles.body:
Greatest league in the world it may be but the Premier League still has its instant forgettables and this was one.

The trampoline sitting beside the main road just two miles from the Stadium of Light, blown there from some poor bairn's garden, said it all about the conditions. That might have been as eventful as the afternoon got.

There was a visible impact of Storm Boelo on the pitch in the first couple minutes, too. Anything aerial was a bit of a lottery. The wind was impossible to work out. One James Trafford long ball held up. Another blew beyond its intended target. In his post-game interview he described the wind as extremely windy and he wasn't wrong.

Players from both sides struggled to hit their mark with passes or deliveries in a scrappy opening. Though Leeds settled better in possession, had more of it and had a couple of moments in and around the box including an off-target Jayden Bogle shot, the first real chance came at the other end. No one got close enough to Brian Brobbey as he picked up the ball for the first time 20 yards out and his bouncing shot had to be palmed round the post by Trafford.

Going long from the back put Dominic Calvert-Lewin in a couple of footraces with Luke O'Nien but by the midway point of the half Leeds could not lay claim to any real danger. Again it was Sunderland and Brobbey who came closest. The hosts almost profited from Harry Wilson's mistaken belief that he had been fouled and Jaka Bijol not getting enough on a back pass, but Trafford came out on top of his one-v-one with Brobbey.

The rest of the half will not live long in the memory. Sunderland cut off angles and took away Leeds' ability to find any joy out wide. It was only through long balls that yellow shirts were able to threaten and it was only really one yellow shirt, that of Calvert-Lewin, that caused Sunderland anything like discomfort. The striker had a shout for a foul by last man O'Nien ignored by the officials and was then denied fair and square by the same defender when another punt forward pitted them against each other.

Though nothing changed in terms of personnel at the interval, Leeds not only spent more time in the Sunderland half in the early stages but began to create at least a little danger. Bogle's cross found Gabriel Gudmundsson at the back stick and he hammered over the crossbar. Tarik Muharemović showed his set-piece magnetism to get on the end of a Wilson corner but headed straight at Robin Roefs. And after Bogle had a shot blocked, James Justin curled one wide.

It wasn't one-way traffic, however. Trafford remained the busier goalkeeper by some distance, throwing himself to both sides of his goal to palm away dangerous strikes. And Sunderland recovered from their shaky start to the half to exert pressure of their own. A corner from the right caused pinball in the Leeds box and a big block was required at the back post.

Momentum swirled back and forth like the crisp packets and litter in and around the technical areas. Back came Leeds. Tanaka's turn and shot forced a save from Roefs and Calvert-Lewin was unable to pounce on the rebound.

Neither side could say they played well, nor could they even really boast of anything like slick passing football. The ball went up and down, up and down, forward and backward. At times it looked beyond the control of anyone out on the pitch. Boots turned into trampolines.

But in the six minutes of time added on Leeds could at least say victory was almost within grasp. Ex-Newcastle United man Sean Longstaff was booed onto the pitch and had the headlines and a silencer on his toe when he drilled at goal from distance, only for Roefs to palm the ball wide. The ball was scrambled into his path in the penalty area and for a brief second the snatch-and-grab was on until his shot hit Lukas Nmecha. A pair of blocked Noah Okafor efforts bookended those chances.

If there was to be a late winner it would have come at that end of the pitch. As a pig of a game was brought to a close no one on the pitch, other than Longstaff perhaps, could feel too aggrieved but Leeds left the Stadium of Light in seventh on 11 points and Sunderland stayed put at the bottom of the table with five.

The positives for the visitors include a clean sheet away from home, a strong display by Trafford and a defensive unit that refuses to give up big chances. Only champions Arsenal have conceded fewer goals. Thanks to those foundations this already has the makings of a solid season. What happens at the other end of the pitch will help decide whether or not solid can be made spectacular.

That is where the improvement could most obviously be made in the performance at Sunderland, but Daniel Farke was keen to point out at full-time that the offence was where the injury disruptions came during the week in training.

The manager felt the point was a good result, as it always should be on the road for a team in their second season of Premier League football. Some points - like the one Leeds secured against third-placed Brighton - look better and better as time goes on. The opposite can be said of others - like the one against Manchester United. However valuable this one looks in retrospect, no one will ever be in a hurry to revisit a windy afternoon on Wearside.

articles.title: European Roundup: Groß denies Wirtz first league goal, Tresoldi scores third hat-trick in a month, ex-Bundesliga defenders scuffle
articles.summary: Florian Wirtz continued his fine form as Liverpool saw off Fabian Hürzeler's Brighton, while Nicolas Tresoldi scored his fourth hat-trick in less than a mont...
articles.body:
Florian Wirtz continued his fine form as Liverpool saw off Fabian Hürzeler 's Brighton, while Nicolas Tresoldi scored his fourth hat-trick in less than a month.

Wirtz's wait for first league goal continues after review, Tel scores wonder goal

Liverpool beat third-placed Brighton a week before hosting defending champions Arsenal at Anfield. Germany international Wirtz thought he finally scored his first Premier League goal of the season, but it was given as an own-goal by his compatriot Pascal Groß after review.

Alexander Isak netted his sixth goal of the campaign as the Reds ended Brighton's six-game winning streak with a 2-0 victory. Fellow former Borussia Dortmund striker Erling Haaland is the only player ahead of the Swedish international in the scorers list, but his ninth strike of the Premier League season wasn't enough for Manchester City against Aston Villa on Saturday afternoon.

Nicolas Jackson , who spent last season on loan at FC Bayern, scored a brace for the Villans as they ended Manchester City's perfect start. Kai Havertz 's Arsenal used the opportunity to level on points with the league leaders as they beat Everton 2-0 at the Emirates.

Arsenal's North London neighbours Tottenham Hotspur also prevailed by the same scoreline at Chelsea. Mathys Tel , who struggled to maintain his promising start at Bayern, scored the "Goal of the Week" with a solo run to seal Spurs' second victory in as many games.

Marco Rose' s Bournemouth achieved the same with a 3-0 rout of out-of-sorts Manchester United, while Newcastle United returned to winning ways at Crystal Palace, which eased the pressure on fellow German coach Matthias Jaissle .

Newcastle United loanee Nick Woltemade finally started a Serie A game as he played the entire game in Juventus' win at Lecce. Former Schalke all-rounder Weston McKennie opened the score with his first goal since April.

AC Milan and Inter also took three points as ex-Bundesliga stars Christian Pulisic and Marcus Thuram scored their clubs' first goals against Udinese and Fiorentina, respectively. The league leaders once again showed their resilence with two injury-time goals to turn it around against relegation-threatened Fiorentina.

Elsewhere, Romano Schmid and Leonardo Balerdi scored braces in high-scoring draws in Italy's top-flight. The former Werder Bremen midfielder had his first Frosinone goals in their 4-4 draw with Atalanta, who had RB Leipzig loanee Eljif Elmas as one of the goalscorers. Balerdi, who had a difficult spell at his first European club Dortmund, netted twice as a substitute to keep AS Roma's unbeaten start with a six-goal thriller at Napoli.

Over in Ligue 1, Tanguy Nianzu , who also struggled during his Bundesliga spell, was sent off in Lille's draw with Monaco, who had Germany U21 international Paris Brunner back from suspension.

Elye Wahi and Mohamed Amoura , who left the Bundesliga on loan last summer, combined for Nice's comeback win against Ludovic Ajorque 's Brest. Thorgan Hazard , who returned to his first professional club after 14 years, scored and assisted in RC Lens' hard-fought win over Paris FC.

The biggest game of the Ligue 1 matchday between PSG and Lyon is postponed for Monday as PSG's superstars will play during the Ballon d'Or ceremony for the second year running.

Mbappe shines as Kane's Ballon d'Or competitors face off in El Clásico

Yan Diomandè helped Real Madrid beat FC Barcelona in El Clásico with a strong performance at Camp Nou. Kylian Mbappé, who is reportedly in the race with Harry Kane and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal, scored a brace for the visitors as he reached 100 Real Madrid goals.

Hansi Flick 's side started the week with a perfect record in all competitions, but they have now lost back-to-back games to Champions League holders PSG and fierce rivals Real Madrid.

On Saturday, Bayer Leverkusen loanee Jeanuel Belocian scored his first LaLiga goal in Racing Santander's comeback win over Espanyol. Over in Eredivisie, Leipzig loanee Lutsharel Geertruida had a memorable game against his former club Feyenoord.

The PSV defender assisted Guus Til 's opening goal before his late winner was canceled for offside. After the game, he was involved in a weird scuffle with his ex-teammate Jeremiah St. Juste , who had a three-year stint in the Bundesliga with Mainz. The two players seemed to be in a friendly mood before they were suddenly involved in a physical battle.

Staying in Dutch's top-tier league, Julian Brandt provided two assists in Ajax's 2-1 win over Sparta Rotterdam. Fellow Germans Marc-Andre ter Stegen and Thilo Kehrer also featured for Ajax as they climbed to second place, with the champions PSV dropping points at home against league leaders Feyenoord.

Peter Bosz 's side will face Club Brugge in their next Champions League encounter. Nicolo Tresoldi , who is yet to decide his international allegiance, scored his second hat-trick for the Belgian champions this month in the 3-2 win over St. Truiden. The 22-year-old striker also had a hat-trick against Malta for Germany U21 during the international break.

Tresoldi leads the scoring chart in Jupiler Pro League with seven goals, alongside Westerlo's Norman Bassette , who spent the second half of last season at 2. Bundesliga side Kaiserslautern.

Former Borussia Mönchengladbach striker Haris Tabakovic tied Christoph Lang with seven goals at the top of Austrian Bundesliga chart after his hat-trick against holders LASK. Elsewhere, Hoffenheim loanee Gift Orban and Mohamed Salah are joint-top-scorers in Turkish Super Lig.

The Nigerian striker scored and assisted in Amedspor's comeback win at ten-man Samsunspor as the newly-promoted side climbed to top before Monday's showdown between Galatasaray and Fenerbahçe.

articles.title: Ballon d'Or 2026: Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal in race for men's award - stats and pundits' opinions
articles.summary: Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe battling for 2026 men's Ballon d'Or on Monday; Kane odds-on favourite to become first Englishman to win the award in 25 years; Lamine Yamal, 19, aiming to become youngest-ever Ballon d'Or winner; Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher backing Kane to win
articles.body:
England captain and Bayern Munich striker Kane is the bookmakers' favourite to become the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001.

Victory would see Kane become just the fifth English winner of the Ballon d'Or after Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen, while he would also become the first Bayern player to claim it in 45 years.

When asked after Bayern's Champions League draw against Arsenal last Wednesday about winning the Ballon d'Or, Kane told Sky Sports News : "It'd be incredible if I do. It'd be special for sure. I'd love to win it, but we will have to wait and see. A big night, but I'm not getting carried away."

Kane's caution comes due to stiff competition from LaLiga duo Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

Spain World Cup winner and Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal, who is 14 years Kane's junior at the age of 19, is aiming to become the youngest-ever Ballon d'Or winner - an award he has been campaigning for.

"Being completely honest, it's not just this year I've been at a Ballon d'Or [winning] level, but longer," he told The Guardian in September, having also appeared to dismiss Kane's credentials earlier that month in a Spanish interview.

Lamine Yamal had been the bookmakers' closest challenger to Kane for the award, but a late surge in the betting means Real Madrid striker and France captain Kylian Mbappe is now second-favourite behind Kane.

A first-time winner looks set to win the award on Monday night, with Kane eyeing a poetic victory in London, where the ceremony is being held to pay tribute to inaugural winner Matthews.

Here, Sky Sports assesses Kane, Lamine Yamal and Mbappe's stats, and hears the pundits' views on who should win the 70th edition of the Ballon d'Or…

It is important to note that players are judged for their performances over the entirety of last season from August 3, 2025 until July 19, 2026.

Looking at that period domestically, Kane helped Bayern to lift the Bundesliga and the German Cup, while Lamine Yamal won LaLiga but missed out on the Copa del Rey as both players won their respective Super Cups.

But Mbappe failed to win a trophy with either Real Madrid or France last season.

In Europe, Kane went further than Lamine Yamal and Mbappe as Bayern reached the Champions League semi-finals after a thrilling 6-5 last-four aggregate defeat to eventual winners Paris Saint-Germain.

Lamine Yamal's Barcelona and Mbappe's Real Madrid both exited the tournament in the quarter-finals.

But Lamine Yamal enjoyed the ultimate success with his country as he helped Spain earn World Cup glory in the summer, while Kane and England won the bronze medal after beating Mbappe's France in the third-place play-off.

The goal statistics are what make Kane the favourite for the award.

He hit an astonishing 73 goals for club and country last season, while Mbappe fired in 58 and Lamine Yamal scored 25 goals.

Kane's goal-laden campaign led to the ex-Tottenham striker picking up the Golden Shoe, the award for Europe's leading goal scorer, for a second time after he claimed it in 2023/24 in his debut Bayern season.

Kane hit 61 goals for Bayern across all competitions last season, 19 more than any other player in Europe's big-five leagues. In fact, it was the most by a player in a season since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014/15.

Kane also scored 12 goals for England, with his six goals in the Three Lions' 2026 World Cup semi-final run seeing him become England's all-time leading World Cup scorer.

But Mbappe scored more goals than Kane at the World Cup and in last season's Champions League.

The ex-PSG forward won this year's World Cup Golden Boot with 10 goals - the most by a player in a single edition since Gerd Muller scored 10 in 1970 for West Germany.

The 27-year-old is now the all-time scorer in World Cup history with 22 goals.

At club level last season, Mbappe was the top goal scorer in LaLiga (25 goals) and in the Champions League, despite Real's last-eight exit, as he scored 15 goals - one more than Kane.

It was a quiet World Cup for Lamine Yamal, scoring only once in Spain's run to glory as team-mates Rodri and Pau Cubarsi picked up the player of the tournament and young player award, respectively.

Lamine Yamal, however, came into his first World Cup off the back of a hamstring injury which had initially led to doubts whether he would even play in the tournament.

Lamine Yamal picked up the injury in mid-April while playing for Barcelona, and he missed the remainder of the season before making his return as a substitute in Spain's goalless draw in their World Cup opener against Cape Verde on June 15, with his first start coming six days later as he scored Spain's first in their win over Saudi Arabia.

Despite his disrupted preparation for the tournament, he made the most dribbles both at the World Cup (58) and across Europe's top-five leagues (265) during the 2025/26 season.

Where Lamine Yamal is superior to Kane and Mbappe is in the assist column.

The winger provided 20 assists for club and country last season, while Mbappe had 13 and Kane had just eight.

It takes Lamine Yamal's goal involvements to 45, but that figure is not close to Kane's 81 and Mbappe's 71.

Jamie Carragher: "Kane should win the Ballon d'Or and the reason is because he's scored 73 goals in a season and only Lionel Messi has scored more in a season.

"He also won the double with Bayern Munich and was part of an England team that got to the World Cup semi-finals."

Paul Merson: "It's such a hard one because Kane's scored a million goals and has been phenomenal, but Lamine Yamal's been phenomenal too and he's won the World Cup.

"But I'm hoping Kane because Lamine Yamal's going to win it three to five times in years to come, so I'd like Kane to win - and it's in London, which ticks another box.

"So I'd just go with Kane, but I wouldn't be shocked if it wasn't him."

Tim Sherwood: "Kane should win the Ballon d'Or - and I'm not being biased. I think he's had an unbelievable season with the amount of goals he's scored for Bayern Munich.

"There's a lot of pressure playing for big club like Bayern, but he never feels the pressure and he continues to score for England. If he doesn't win it now, then he never will."

Sue Smith: "Kane has got to win the Ballon d'Or. He's been absolutely brilliant. His goals, his movement, the way he drops into the No.10, the ability he's got and he's been outstandingly consistency."

Michael Dawson: "I believe it should be Kane. I'm probably slightly biased as I was lucky to play with him. The goals and everything he's given in the last year, he has to be the winner but Lamine Yamal is the guy he has to beat."

Clinton Morrison: "Kane should win because he's had a fantastic season at Bayern Munich and he leads England by example. Lamine Yamal and Michael Olise could dominate for years to come, but Kane thoroughly deserves it this year."

A third year in a row for a first-time winner?

Should Kane, Mbappe or Lamine Yamal be crowned the Ballon d'Or winner, it will be a third year running a new name has been awarded the gong after years of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo dominance.

Take a look at the previous winners below, as well as other historical stats from the award's history...

The men's Ballon dO'r shortlist in full...

articles.title: El palo de Pepe Brasín al Barcelona tras caer ante el Madrid: "Nació el Barça real de esta temporada"
articles.standfirst: El analista destaca la resurrección del equipo blanco y señala las dudas defensivas de un Barcelona que ha perdido ante el PSG y el Madrid
articles.summary: El analista destaca la resurrección del equipo blanco y señala las dudas defensivas de un Barcelona que ha perdido ante el PSG y el Madrid
articles.body: El Clásico ha cambiado el panorama de la Liga. Pepe Brasín, en su conversación con Raúl Varela en Las brasas de Brasín, puso el foco en la reacción del Real Madrid y en los problemas que han aparecido en el Barcelona tras sus últimos tropiezos. "Mi conclusión es favorable al Real Madrid más que negativa sobre el Barça", resumió Brasín, que considera que el conjunto blanco ha dado un paso adelante en las últimas semanas. Brasín lleva tiempo defendiendo que el equipo madridista ha encontrado una nueva identidad. Su actuación en el Camp Nou reforzó esa impresión. "El Real Madrid hace un partido, a mi gusto, soberbio", afirmó. El analista fue todavía más contundente al valorar el resultado: "Gana bien, es mejor equipo que el Barça ayer y se pone a tres en la Liga". En su opinión, el mérito del Madrid está por encima de los problemas azulgranas. "El Real Madrid lleva 15 días redescubriéndose a sí mismo", explicó, destacando la capacidad del equipo para aprovechar las cualidades de su plantilla. En el lado azulgrana, Brasín señaló el cambio de sensaciones tras los partidos ante el PSG y el Real Madrid. "Probablemente en París nació otro Barça", apuntó, antes de añadir: "Nació el Barça real de esta temporada". El comentarista considera que los rivales de mayor nivel han puesto en evidencia unas debilidades que hasta ahora quedaban disimuladas por los resultados. "Sí que es un equipo que se genera dudas a sí mismo, que se mira en el espejo y que ya no se ve tan guapo", afirmó. Brasín también puso el foco en los problemas defensivos del equipo de Hansi Flick: "Todos esos problemas defensivos que creíamos que podían existir sobre el papel aparecen frente al París Saint-Germain y aparecen frente al Real Madrid".

articles.title: Mourinho talks Cucurella, Diomande, Camavinga, Bernardo, Lunin after Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho had plenty to celebrate after Real Madrid secured a 2-1 victory over Barcelona in the first El Clasico of the 2026/27 season, but the Portugues...
articles.body:
Jose Mourinho had plenty to celebrate after Real Madrid secured a 2-1 victory over Barcelona in the first El Clasico of the 2026/27 season, but the Portuguese manager also found time to deliver a cheeky message to the home supporters.

Speaking after the match, Mourinho joked that Barcelona fans had prevented him from taking his usual afternoon nap before the game, before explaining how his tactical decisions, squad depth and Eduardo Camavinga's decisive contribution helped Madrid secure the win.

The Real Madrid manager also praised Marc Cucurella for his performance against Lamine Yamal, highlighted Yan Diomande's defensive contribution and backed Andriy Lunin after the goalkeeper stepped in for Thibaut Courtois.

Mourinho takes a playful dig at Barcelona fans

Mourinho opened his post-match comments by dedicating the victory to the Barcelona supporters whose singing outside the team hotel had disrupted his rest before the game.

"I dedicate this win to the Barca fans that did not let me take my nap in the hotel today.

"They came to the hotel and they kept singing all day, so I couldn't take my nap. Well, I didn't nap, but I did beat their team. A big hug to them."

The remark captured Mourinho's ability to add personality to a major victory.

More importantly for Real Madrid, the result gave his team a significant psychological boost in a fixture that can have consequences well beyond the three points on offer.

Mourinho also praised Cucurella's discipline against Yamal and credited Diomande for limiting Barcelona's options on the opposite flank.

Mourinho had nothing but praise for Cucurella. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

"We've got two top-class left-backs, which means I can rotate them a bit. Carreras played on Wednesday, and that allowed Cucu to be fresh, focused and thinking only about this match.

"Obviously he was up against a great player, but he's his teammate and knows him well.

"I always say that I only really understand how good players are when I see them right in front of me – when I'm on the touchline.

"He is very good, but he's also clever. He tried everything to get Cucu booked, but Cucu held his ground well, and Diomande very rarely let Espart or Cancelo get the better of him.

"A great team effort. But Cucu… he was excellent against a very good opponent."

Mourinho explains midfield balance and Camavinga decision

Real Madrid's tactical adjustments were another major talking point.

Mourinho explained that the team's recent performances had reinforced his belief in combining midfielders with different strengths rather than relying on players with similar characteristics.

"That I have an extraordinary squad, with every player possessing the quality and mentality to play.

"I've learnt that in midfield… having a mix of talents gives us more than having two players with similar characteristics.

"And by that I mean that the Bernardo-Güler double pivot… I don't use it. Or only in desperate situations.

"But the double pivot we finished with today – Camavinga and Tchouameni – will also only be used at specific moments. I'm enjoying it.

"I think the people at the top like this mix too, because it gives us balance in defence and more quality when it comes to building from the back."

Camavinga played a crucial role in Real Madrid's match-winning goal. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Mourinho then detailed why Camavinga's introduction proved important, particularly after Barcelona brought Frenkie de Jong onto the pitch.

The Madrid manager wanted fresh legs to sustain the press and exploit openings during transitions, with Camavinga instructed to attack spaces from deeper positions.

"Camavinga, like everyone else, is a first-team player. There are times when you want to make substitutions; you look at the bench, and many managers suffer because they have no options, because they're unable to implement their ideas. But I've got a strong bench.

"Camavinga had an extraordinary match against Leipzig; today he was on the bench. Flick brought on De Jong, who's a real powerhouse, to face Bernardo, who'd been working hard against Pedri for a long time…

"The match needed fresh legs to keep up the pressing and to launch counter-attacks.

"And I told Camavinga that, obviously, it was Tchouameni who was covering that position due to his attributes and having picked up a yellow card… and that he had to attack the spaces – something that's difficult against Barcelona, because often you attack and you're offside or the goalkeeper is off his line.

"If the run comes from the second line, as Camavinga did, it's more difficult for them. Things went well. A great match; the team deserved more."

Mourinho backs Lunin and refuses to declare a first choice team

Asked whether the victory could prove a turning point in the season, Mourinho emphasised both the psychological importance of the result and the manner in which Real Madrid earned it.

Andriy Lunin put on a great performance vs Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

"This was a match where we could have come away with three, six or nine points. Obviously, if you come away with nine, it's a psychological burden.

"The way we won is also different. Because you can win with a bit of luck, but we did it calmly and fully deserved it."

The manager also insisted that his starting lineup would remain flexible, pointing to the quality and competitiveness within the squad.

He used the discussion around Bernardo's selection to explain why he would not commit to a fixed first-choice team.

"On the selection of Bernardo… I've only been here a little over three months. And although I know him well, that's one thing; knowing how he can slot into the team's dynamics is quite another.

"The squad is very strong. I'll never say that this is my first-choice team or that this line-up is set in stone, because the squad is very good and well-rounded. The lads work hard. Everyone is ready.

"And that's just how it is. You've already asked me two questions and neither was about Lunin, but if we lose here because of mistakes he makes, the first or second question would be about him.

"I've only said to him, 'You train to play, not to sit on the bench; go and play.' And he's put in a performance with great composure and poise.

"We have the best goalkeeper in the world, but today none of us has been upset that Thibaut isn't playing," he concluded.

articles.title: Ballon d’Or 2026 power rankings: Who leads race ahead of tonight’s ceremony
articles.summary: Here’s how the top 10 contenders, including Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal, rank in the race to lift the Ballon d’Or ahead of tonight’s ceremony
articles.body:
The race for the Ballon d'Or is all but over with the world's best player set to be crowned in the glamorous London ceremony this evening.

Harry Kane , Lamine Yamal and others have made their case, with a campaign from players, clubs and entourages filling pages and social media feeds for weeks.

Spain's triumph over Argentina in the World Cup final catapulted 2024 winner Rodri and Yamal into contention, though Barcelona pushed for the latter as their main contender, potentially avoiding a share of votes between the two international and club colleagues.

Kane is the favourite , according to the bookmakers, and the Bayern Munich and England forward's case is built behind a relentless run of production, both scoring and creating goals, to twist the narrative in his favour.

During the World Cup, eight-time Ballon d'Or winner Lionel Messi showed that he can still force himself into the conversation at the age of 39, firing eight goals to propel Argentina to the final and briefly take the crown as the competition's all-time top goalscorer - until he was eclipsed by Kylian Mbappe , while Sir David Beckham has tipped the Argentine to win after inspiring Inter Miami to the Campeones Cup. Here's how the top 10 front-runners stack up in The Independent's Ballon d'Or 2026 power rankings:

What's this, a new entry to the power rankings?! Barcelona's Cubarsi is favourite to bring home the Golden Boy award, but he's so far been bumped from our list by Vinicius Jr, who squeezed into our top 10 mainly to spare myself some angry emails from those affiliated to Real Madrid and Brazil (I joke, kind of).

The 2024 runner-up had another strong season at the Bernabeu, netting 22 goals in 36 appearances, though was unable to inspire the club to a trophy. And after a below average start to the new term, with just one goal to his name in 10 as Real sit six points off the top, he's been usurped by an El Clasico rival in Cubarsi.

Despite still only being 19, Cubarsi is an established figure at the heart of the Barca and Spain defence, and after picking up the honour of Young Player of the Tournament following his country's World Cup win, he has carried that impenetrable form back to the Camp Nou. The Blaugrana have won nine from nine in the league and haven't looked close to suffering defeat.

He's up there among the best defenders on the planet as a teenager, playing a role that usually favours the more experienced; he will only get better. But does that mean Cubarsi will become the second player to ever win both the Golden Boy and Ballon d'Or on the same night after Messi? Doubtful.

Crystal Palace could only keep him in Croydon for so long.

With Bayern Munich and France, Olise has established himself as one of the world's best attackers, a talent so bright that the German giants did well to ward off interest from the likes of Real Madrid - who no doubt saw the World Cup partnership he formed with Mbappe and want to reunite the pair in the Spanish capital at some stage.

Will his electrifying performances be enough to win the Ballon d'Or? Probably not, this year. But he's in the conversation, which is a statement in itself.

The jury may also fear what an Olise acceptance speech might look like. If his post-match interview from Bayern's opening Champions League win over Bodo/Glimt is anything to go by, in which he scored a brace and assisted another, it'll be like getting blood out of a stone. The perils of the nonchalant gimmick.

For unrivalled football insight from Miguel Delaney, join Inside Football here .

On solely his performances, Haaland does not exactly deserve to drop down in these rankings as we hurtle towards the Ballon d'Or ceremony. So let's start with the good.

In the summer, Haaland was one of the stars of the World Cup and ensured Norway, playing in their first finals since 1998, lived up to their dark-horse status by powering them to the last-eight. On the way, his unrelenting goalscoring exploits humbled Brazil , sending the five-time winners packing. Away from the big-hitting nations, Haaland was far and away the tournament's standout player, to little surprise.

He has then followed up on a pretty bog-standard season for City - just the 38 goals last year, the fourth season he's hit 30+ at the Etihad, and a domestic double - by starting the season with 12 goals in 10 appearances. The man can't and won't stop scoring.

But, there's a big but. Voting for the Ballon d'Or closed a few days after City's guilty verdict was revealed. Currently, every bit of success related that club feels tainted. We feel that would have swayed some on the jury (not all) to vote against Haaland, whose goals are being financed by owners who inflated their own sponsorship income by £830m across eight seasons. He was already an outsider, but his odds have dropped further.

How was this man's place on the England plane ever in question?! Thomas Tuchel's player of the tournament, Bellingham served his critics a serious helping of humble pie by guiding the Three Lions to the elusive World Cup bronze.

That beautiful redemption arc , on its own, got Bellingham onto this list. That's because the season that preceded the World Cup wasn't spectacular. Injuries limited him to just 13 goal contributions for Real Madrid in another trophyless campaign.

However, he's started the new season pretty well, and that keeps him on this list - seven goal contributions in nine league games shows he might be returning to his Madrid form of old under Jose Mourinho. He also just bagged four goal contributions in England's 7-0 thumping of Croatia, the first midfielder to do so in a single match for the Three Lions since David Platt scored four against San Marino in February 1993.

His chances of winning the Ballon d'Or are still low compared to the competition. But as was proved at the World Cup - maybe don't count him out.

Had France won the World Cup, as many expected them to do leading up to that drab semi-final exit , Dembele would have been heavily favoured to secure a second successive Ballon d'Or. The combination of World Cup and Champions League winners' medals is a bit of a cheat code.

That would've been quite the gimme for a player who, let's be honest, was France's fourth best attacker at the World Cup. And while, like last year, he ended the season as Paris Saint-Germain's top scorer with a Ligue 1 and Champions League to boot, he only managed about half of his goalscoring output.

His trophy haul still carries enough weight to be comfortably in the top 10 contenders, but the failure to lift that World Cup title gives him only an outside chance to go back-to-back - and we think that's fair. His slow start to the new campaign, only scoring his first league goal last weekend, doesn't help his cause. Sorry Ousmane, but this year shouldn't be your year.

He couldn't again, could he? Messi's inclusion on this list encapsulates the significance of the World Cup in deciding the Ballon d'Or winner; he's not going to take the accolade for his MLS exploits, is he. But fair play to the eight-time winner; at 39, he showed he very much still had it.

Messi's eight goals propelled Argentina to the World Cup final, where they were rightly defeated by Spain - had he lifted back-to-back titles, he'd probably be towards the top two of this list. After all, he claimed the 2023 award after La Albiceleste's triumph 10 months earlier, by which time he was on the books at Inter Miami.

Even with his runners-up medal, Indy Sport writers had him as the player of the tournament . That, combined with the jury's historic love for the Argentinian, means you can't exactly write him off. Messi's retirement from international football , announced following the death of his father, Jorge, underlines that this is now his final chance to win another Ballon d'Or.

Beckham has tipped him to do just that after helping Inter Miami to the Campeones Cup. I'm sure the jury will put adequate weight on that...

It feels pretty crazy to think that, at 27, Mbappe still doesn't have a Ballon d'Or to his name, given he's been at the top of the game for what feels like forever now.

Once again, he's very much a frontrunner time around. His Golden Boot at the World Cup will do most of the heavy lifting, with his 10 goals in North America seeing him pass first Miroslav Klose and then Lionel Messi as the tournament's all-time record goalscorer. Both he and Messi would have felt hard done by not to go home with the Golden Ball.

But lest we forget, despite the toxicity that surrounded his club season with Real Madrid, he didn't exactly experience a drop-off in performance. He bagged 42 goals in 44 games, all while being hounded at the Bernabeu - and while it wasn't enough to prevent another trophyless season for Los Blancos , you can't knock his output.

Mbappe still believes he is the best in the world and under Mourinho , he's crucially got the new season off to a flyer. He is already in scintillating goalscoring form, bagging 12 in 12, and suddenly looks one of the biggest challengers for the fabled individual prize.

You might not like it, but the weight of the World Cup in the eyes of the Ballon d'Or jury is undeniable. Just ask Luka Modric.

Rodri had a sensational World Cup at the heart of Spain's midfield, shielding their rock-solid defence while acting as the metronome that took play forward. His influence took him to the Golden Ball ahead of top goalscorers Messi and Mbappe - and in the immediate aftermath, we felt that could be enough to swing the Ballon d'Or in his favour.

That always felt like a bit of an injustice, considering he didn't have the most spectacular domestic season. Returning from injury with Manchester City, it took him a while to properly find his feet in a campaign that saw Pep Guardiola's side win the FA Cup and League Cup, but miss out on the Premier League title.

Yes, the World Cup is the World Cup - and whether you agree with the importance of team achievements in an individual award, the reality is that it does matter a hell of a lot. What could tip the scales further in his favour, though, is his start to life at Barcelona. He's slotted into a team that have began the new season in staggering form, with a 100 percent record in the league and +30 goal difference after just nine games.

That said, he doesn't seem full of self-belief, instead feeling that Barcelona are pushing team-mate Yamal to win the award. "The club has opted for Lamine because they believe he is the player who deserves it most, and that's perfectly legitimate," he said.

Yamal will surely win his fair share of Ballon d'Ors across his career, but the 19-year-old may very well end up taking home his first this year, going one better than his runners-up finish in 2025.

He became the first player under 20 to appear at both a European Championship final and a World Cup final - he won both. While his output was pretty modest for his standards, he was influential throughout the tournament for Spain - and that's after coming into it carrying a hamstring injury.

But unlike team-mate Rodri, who sits below him in these rankings, his club form across the past year enhances his argument to win the award rather than detracts from it. He bagged 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions for Barcelona in another LaLiga-winning season - hardly mediocre numbers - and has started the new term with 20 goal contributions in 12 games, contributing to Barca's eye-watering goal difference early doors.

It's back on Spain duty, though, where Yamal made a statement in his Ballon d'Or joust with Kane. A Nations League showdown between the pair at Wembley was won by Yamal, who scored inside two minutes when taking advantage of a Marc Guehi error. Spain went on to win 3-2 , with Kane missing a crucial penalty.

This happened a couple of days before voting for the Ballon d'Or closed. Might it have convinced some of the jury to go another way? It briefly made Yamal the odds-on favourite for the award - but a certain Englishman has since returned to the top of the pile...

England captain Kane is the frontrunner to win the Ballon d'Or despite failing to set the World Cup alight quite like he managed the Bundesliga in 2025/26. That's a testament to just how prolific he was last term.

Kane was the top goalscorer in Europe, hitting 61 goals in 51 games across all competitions as he spearheaded Bayern towards the league and cup double; he's added silverware to his ever-present individual numbers. He was then hardly irrelevant at the World Cup, scoring six goals - including a crucial late brace against DR Congo to spare his country serious embarrassment - as England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 .

After a similarly strong start to the new season, recording 17 goal contributions in 11 appearances, the jury has good reason to put their classic emphasis on the World Cup and wider team achievement to one side. There is also the significance of the location of the Ballon d'Or ceremony to consider; it will be held in London, to commemorate the 70th anniversary of the very first Ballon d'Or won by England's Sir Stanley Matthews. Could Kane become just the fifth Englishman to win the prize?

His England team-mate Declan Rice certainly thinks so. "For me, he's the clear winner," Rice said after Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Bayern . "I think his numbers speak for himself. The year he's had has been remarkable."

articles.title: Pennant has more than 50 stitches after dog attack
articles.summary: Former Premier League footballer Jermaine Pennant says he needed more than 50 stitches after being mauled by a dog.
articles.body:
Former Premier League footballer Jermaine Pennant says he needed more than 50 stitches after being mauled by a dog.

The 43-year-old was walking his two dogs in north London last week when he was attacked by a German Shepherd.

The former Liverpool and Stoke City winger said the dog latched on to his leg and refused to let go as he tried to protect his own dog, King.

King then intervened to help fight off the attacking dog, preventing "what could've been an horrendous situation", Pennant said in a post on Instagram.

Pennant told the Sun he required more than 50 stitches to his right leg after sustaining four bite wounds in the attack and receiving hospital treatment.

He added that King was unhurt, but did not give details about the German Shepherd. He said he declined to report the attack to police.

"So I was attacked by a German shepherd, I tried to protect King but the dog got my leg, I was on the floor with the dog still attached with no sign of letting go, until King intervened as he didn't know what was going on," said Pennant.

"But the minute he did he fought the dog off and saved what could've been a horrendous situation for me.

"King was unhurt with a little nip on his leg, but had blood covered all over him which wasn't mine. At this point I forgot the agony I was in, and my heart sank, but it wasn't King's."

The picture uploaded to Instagram shows Pennant with a bandage on his leg alongside King on a sofa, while he also thanked his partner Mimmi Montgomery for looking after them.

"My hero still protecting me and trying to look after me. King you're a legend, love you, man's best friend. Thanks Mimmi Montgomery for taking care of us both."

Pennant, who is a pundit for Talksport, made 231 Premier League appearances in a 19-year career before retiring in 2018.

articles.title: Roberto Gómez señala al gran triunfador del Clásico: "¿Dónde está Mourinho cuestionado?"
articles.standfirst: El periodista ensalza la actuación del Real Madrid en el Camp Nou, carga contra quienes daban la Liga por sentenciada y considera que el técnico madridista fue el gran protagonista de la victoria
articles.summary: El periodista ensalza la actuación del Real Madrid en el Camp Nou, carga contra quienes daban la Liga por sentenciada y considera que el técnico madridista fue el gran protagonista de la victoria
articles.body: Roberto Gómez no se mordió la lengua tras la victoria del Real Madrid ante el Barcelona en el Camp Nou. En su intervención en La Tribu, con Raúl Varela, el periodista defendió el partido del conjunto blanco, reivindicó el trabajo de José Mourinho y recordó las críticas que había recibido el equipo en los días previos al Clásico. "¿Dónde están los que le van a caer seis? ¿Dónde se acabó la Liga? ¿Dónde Mourinho cuestionado? ¿Dónde Mbappé prácticamente irrelevante?", lanzó Roberto Gómez, visiblemente molesto con los pronósticos que daban por descontada una victoria azulgrana. Para el periodista, la victoria madridista tuvo un protagonista por encima del resto: su entrenador. "Para mí espectacular en la alineación, en la dirección del partido y, sobre todo, lo que es más importante, que sabía cómo tenía que jugar al Barcelona", afirmó. Roberto Gómez insistió en su argumento durante el debate: "¿Por qué os cuesta tanto reconocer que ayer el que le da un repaso a Flick es Mourinho?". El periodista también defendió el rendimiento colectivo del Madrid y destacó la actuación de Mbappé y las intervenciones del guardameta madridista en ausencia de Courtois. A su juicio, el equipo respondió en un escenario de máxima exigencia después de las dudas que había generado durante las semanas anteriores. Gómez cargó contra quienes habían cuestionado la capacidad competitiva del conjunto blanco antes del Clásico. "Se le ha faltado el respeto, se le ha ninguneado mucho a este equipo", aseguró El periodista, no obstante, evitó dar por decidida la lucha por el campeonato. "Yo no sé si el Madrid va a ganar la Liga, porque no soy futurólogo", reconoció.
